question: Should remotely bound Telegram and Zalo servers reject only private/link-local webhook targets as currently documented, or enforce the PR's broader global-only destination policy including rejection of public IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals?
rationale: Both policies are defensible security postures, but the broader policy intentionally changes existing behavior and provider-visible errors, so maintainer intent is required before merge.

options.title: Adopt global-only policy
options.body: Update names, errors, and setup documentation to state the broader contract and provide live upgrade proof for representative accepted and rejected targets.

options.title: Preserve current contract
options.body: Keep blocking private and link-local destinations while classifying embedded IPv4 values so globally reachable mapped targets remain allowed.

options.title: Split webhook policy
options.body: Land the independent runtime hardening and review the destination-policy change separately.

recommendation.title: Adopt global-only policy
recommendation.body: Update names, errors, and setup documentation to state the broader contract and provide live upgrade proof for representative accepted and rejected targets.
